items.headline: Kairos lines up $643M for Hermes 2 in Tennessee, $275M from DOE
items.what_happened: Kairos Power has lined up a $643 million funding package for its Tennessee reactor program, according to a Bloomberg report on October 14, 2026. It includes $368 million from private backers and $275 million in U.S. Department of Energy financing. Kairos expects the 50 MW Hermes 2 demonstration plant in Oak Ridge to start up in 2030.
items.why_it_matters: Hermes 2 is a 50 MWe plant, above the 1-20 MW range this site tracks. It is a read on how much capital and federal money a non-light-water design now needs, and on whether DOE support is reaching commercial-scale builds.
items.binding_note: Reported as lined up or secured, but no closing agreement, DOE loan or award document, or Kairos release was found. Secondary coverage differs on how the private $368 million is split among investors. The Samsung C&T $70 million is separate and already shipped.

items.headline: DOE picks Deployable Energy's Unity nuclear battery for 2027 DOME test
items.what_happened: DOE's National Reactor Innovation Center selected Deployable Energy to test its Unity nuclear battery in the DOME testbed at Idaho National Laboratory in 2027. The test is planned to start in May 2027 and run for up to six months. Deployable announced the selection on October 7, 2026.
items.why_it_matters: A DOME slot gives a transportable reactor design access to federal test infrastructure. It is an access selection, not a purchase, and the source gives no agreement value or terms.
items.binding_note: A DOE selection for a test slot in 2027. No test agreement or contract terms are published, and the test has not started.
